identity.title: MGD$^3$ : Mode-Guided Dataset Distillation using Diffusion Models

problem.claim: Reduce training and deployment costs through dataset distillation while preserving useful data diversity.

gap.claim: Existing generative distillation methods require fine-tuning with distillation losses, yet do not guarantee sample diversity, limiting performance.

contributions.claim: A mode-guided diffusion approach that uses a pre-trained diffusion model without fine-tuning with distillation losses.
A three-stage process—Mode Discovery, Mode Guidance, and Stop Guidance—to address mode coverage, intra-class diversity, and synthetic artifacts.
Reported accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art methods on four image benchmarks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by avoiding diffusion-model fine-tuning with distillation losses while explicitly guiding modes and stopping guidance to reduce artifacts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report accuracy gains of 4.4%, 2.9%, 1.6%, and 1.6% on ImageNette, ImageIDC, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1K, respectively, over state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that eliminating distillation-loss fine-tuning significantly reduces computational costs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dataset distillation is presented as a way to reduce training costs and support efficient deployment by capturing data distributions with generative models.
Prior methods rely on fine-tuning and still lack guaranteed sample diversity.
The paper proposes mode-guided diffusion with three stages targeting mode discovery, intra-class diversity, and artifact mitigation.
The authors report accuracy gains across four image benchmarks and lower computational costs from avoiding fine-tuning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps three named procedural stages to distinct diversity or quality problems: mode discovery, intra-class diversity, and artifacts.

lessons.interpretation: This links each method component to a concrete failure mode, making the claimed mechanism easier to inspect.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-stage method, pair every stage with the specific data or model failure it is intended to address.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when stages are tightly coupled and cannot be meaningfully assigned separate roles.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset-distillation budgets, evaluation protocols, baseline identities, statistical variation, or whether the reported accuracy gains are absolute or relative.
The computational-cost reduction is described qualitatively without measurements or hardware conditions.
